upstreamProbe: GitHub commits API answers 422 {"message":"No commit found for SHA: <prefix>"} for all four prefixes, so no upstream object exists under them (probed by the maintainer; not re-probed here).
decision: A: substitute the subject-matched 40-hex from the local mirror and record the provenance, instead of keeping an unresolvable 10-hex prefix.
why: A 10-hex prefix that no upstream resolves is a dangling identifier: anyone auditing the ledger gets 422 and cannot verify the entry.
The subject is byte-identical in the local mirror, so the change is auditable today with git cat-file / git log in a checkout every lane already has.
Keeping the prefix would require the baseline to keep asserting 'must be backfilled from the authoritative mirror', which is provably impossible.
consequences: parity/commits.json: sha40 3673 -> 3677, prefixOnly10 []; each of the four entries carries an appended evidence sentence naming the prefix, the 422, and the substituted digest.

parity/baseline.json: the old blocker ('absent from the local mirror, must be backfilled') is replaced by a blocker that states these four are subject-identified and must not be read as GitHub-compare entries.
These four must not be used to reconcile a git range: they are not ancestors of the anchor unless resolvedShaIsAncestorOfAnchor says so.
